items.text: Forensic science career options span eight real tracks: biology/DNA, digital forensics, forensic accounting, toxicology, ballistics, documents, psychology, and anthropology/odontology.
The most common entry point, filled through a state recruitment exam (UPSSSC, a state PSC, or a department-specific test), not a campus placement.
Requires clearing a genuinely competitive written exam plus interview, usually after an NFSU or other recognised forensic science degree.

This is the track most forensic science career searches never surface, because it is filed under "cybersecurity" as often as "forensic science." It is also, by pay and by employer growth, the strongest track on this entire list right now.
Entry-level work: imaging drives, extracting call/chat logs, and running first-pass analysis under a senior analyst's review.
Owns full case investigations end to end: mobile and cloud forensics, malware triage, and writing reports built to survive cross-examination in court.
Toxicology, ballistics, and questioned documents follow the same four-rung government FSL ladder described above.
Analyses blood, viscera, and other samples for poisons, drugs, and alcohol in suspicious-death and NDPS (narcotics) cases.

A B.Sc or M.Sc Forensic Science from a private college teaches the same core subjects regardless of college, but only a genuinely recognised degree, and a cleared recruitment exam, gets you into a government FSL seat.
That single image covers maybe two of the eight tracks above.
The real Indian job market for this specific specialisation is thin.
